To determine whether the proposed solution is correct, let us test the case $N = 1$, which corresponds to a $3 \times 3 \times 3$ cube:

The proposed solution claims the maximum number of black cubes is:
$$\frac{(2N+1)^3 + 1}{2} = \frac{3^3 + 1}{2} = 14$$

However, consider coloring the cube in layers along the $z$-axis ($z \in \{1, 2, 3\}$):
- Layer $z = 1$: all 9 unit cubes are black.
- Layer $z = 2$: all 9 unit cubes are white.
- Layer $z = 3$: all 9 unit cubes are black.

Every $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cube must intersect two consecutive layers (either layers $\{1, 2\}$ or layers $\{2, 3\}$):
- A $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cube intersecting layers 1 and 2 contains 4 black cubes from layer 1 and 4 white cubes from layer 2, giving exactly 4 black cubes.
- A $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cube intersecting layers 2 and 3 contains 4 white cubes from layer 2 and 4 black cubes from layer 3, giving exactly 4 black cubes.

This configuration strictly satisfies the condition that every $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cube contains at most 4 black cubes, yet it uses:
$$9 + 0 + 9 = 18 \text{ black cubes}$$

Since $18 > 14$, the proposed maximum is incorrect.

VERDICT: REJECT
